S35.01.needs: a paid account (a Free account sees the Upgrade to use Deep Research message)
S35.01.note: The visible name of the + button itself was not found in the code; the menu row label is confirmed.
steps: Open the + menu under the chat box.
Click Deep Research so it is switched on.
Type a research question and press send.
Look for the Deep research status card in the reply, showing a phase such as Planning research.
S35.01.where: Composer > + menu > Deep Research, then send a question

steps: Turn on Deep Research and send a question.
When the Research plan card appears, find the Deliverable box.
Pick Executive summary or Full report.
Open the Format list and pick a format such as Bullet brief, then compare with the choices shown in Expected.
S35.02.where: Composer > + menu > Deep Research, send a question > Research plan card > Deliverable

S35.04.note: The plan card only appears while the run is waiting for approval.
steps: Send a Deep Research question and wait for the Research plan card.
Change the words in a step box (Research step 1, 2...).
Click Add a step, or click the X beside a step to remove it.
Click Start research and check that the searches follow the edited steps.
S35.04.where: Research plan card (shown after sending a Deep Research question) > Add a step / Remove this step / Start research

S35.05.needs: a paid account; for Connected app, a connected work app
steps: On the Research plan card, open the Add a source list.
Choose a kind: Only this site, Never this site, My files or Connected app.
Click Add.
Look for the chip under Sources for this run, or the text Searching the whole web. Add a source to narrow it. when the list is empty.
S35.05.where: Research plan card > Add a source > My files / Only this site / Never this site / Connected app > Add

S35.06.note: Enforcement happens on the server; the code I read does not show how a run is judged against the rule.
steps: On the Research plan card, set Add a source to Only this site or Never this site.
Type a domain in the Site to add box (placeholder nature.com, who.int) and press Enter, or click Add.
Look for the chip, which reads Never plus the domain for a restricted site.
Start the run and compare the report's sources with the chosen site rule.
S35.06.where: Research plan card > Add a source > Only this site or Never this site, then type a site > Add

S35.07.needs: a paid account, a file to upload
S35.07.note: The card adds a My files source, but I found no file picker in this component; where the files are chosen was not confirmed.
steps: On the Research plan card, set Add a source to My files.
Click Add.
Look for the My files chip under Sources for this run.
Start the run and check that the report cites your uploaded material.
S35.07.where: Research plan card > Add a source > My files > Add

S35.08.needs: a paid account, a connected work app (such as Drive or Slack); the option only appears when an app is connected
S35.08.note: How an app gets connected was not confirmed in this file.
steps: On the Research plan card, set Add a source to Connected app.
Open the Choose an app list and pick a connected app.
Click Add.
Look for the app's name as a chip under Sources for this run.
S35.08.where: Research plan card > Add a source > Connected app > Choose an app > Add

S35.09.note: Counts only appear once they are above zero.
steps: Start a Deep Research run and watch the status bar of the reply.
Read the phase text, such as Planning research, Searching the web or Writing report.
Read the counts on the right: searches and sources, and the elapsed time (m:ss).
Check that the counts go up while the run is working.
S35.09.where: Chat reply > Deep research status card (above the answer)

S35.10.note: This is a step list with status words, not a dated timeline. The status words for running and queued come from runStatusLabel, which I did not open, so their exact wording is unverified.
steps: Start a Deep Research run and let it work.
Look at the list under the status bar, labelled Research plan.
Read the status word on each step, and Not run on steps that were dropped.
Compare with the steps as they run.
S35.10.where: Deep research status card > Research plan step list under the status bar

S35.11.needs: a paid account, a finished or running Deep Research answer
steps: Under a Deep Research answer, click the View N sources button.
In the side panel, check that the Sources tab is selected.
Read the Citations and More lists.
Compare the list with the sources the run visited.
S35.11.where: Under the answer, click View N sources (or the globe button titled Research sources) > Sources tab

S35.12.needs: a paid account, a finished Deep Research answer
S35.12.note: Excerpts appear only when the source has one; I did not confirm the excerpt display in the row markup.
steps: Open the Sources tab of the research side panel.
Click or read a source row: the host, the Published and Retrieved dates, and the excerpt.
Compare the evidence excerpts with the report's statements.
S35.12.where: Research side panel > Sources tab (open from View N sources)

S35.13.needs: a paid account, a finished report with planned questions
S35.13.note: The code shows questions with their status, not findings grouped under each question.
steps: Open a finished report in the Report tab.
Find the section headed Planned questions.
Read each line marked Answered or Not answered, and the reason under open questions.
Compare with the report body.
S35.13.where: Research side panel > Report tab > Planned questions

labels.text: Add a focus, a question or a source to cover

S35.15.needs: a paid account, a run that is still searching
steps: While the run is searching, click Steer.
Type in the box Add a focus, a question or a source to cover.
Click Send.
Look for the line Your guidance is applied when the current step finishes, and the plan updates to follow it.

S35.17.needs: a paid account, a run that is still searching
steps: While the run is searching, click Pause.
Wait for the label to read Pausing… and then the status to read Research paused.
Click Resume (optionally type guidance in the box next to it).
Check that the run continues from the step it stopped at.
S35.17.where: Deep research status card > Pause, then Resume

S35.18.note: I did not confirm that the composer stop button also records the run as cancelled; the plan Cancel path does set the phase to interrupted.
steps: Start a Deep Research run.
Click the stop button in the composer while the run works, or click Cancel on the Research plan card before it searches.
Look for the status Research stopped and the note (stopped by you).
Check that the run no longer adds searches.
S35.18.where: Composer > Stop the current response (tooltip Stop generation) during a run; or Research plan card > Cancel before searching starts

S35.19.needs: a paid account, a run that is stopped before the report is written
S35.19.note: The partial-report banner text is built from the report status; the word partial was not found in the report view code, so the label wording is unverified.
steps: Stop a Deep Research run after some searching has happened.
Open its report from the Report tab.
Read the banner under the title, which begins This report is followed by the report status.
Check that the report has the material gathered before the stop.
S35.19.where: Research side panel > Report tab (or Library) > report banner after a stopped run

S35.20.needs: a paid account, a finished report
steps: Open a finished report in the Report tab.
Check the title, the summary, the body and the sources.
Click Read report full screen to open the reader at full size.
S35.20.where: Under the answer, View N sources > Report tab (or Library > open a report) > Read report full screen

S35.21.needs: a paid account, a finished report with three or more headings
steps: Open a finished report with at least three headings.
Look for the box titled Contents.
Click one heading in the list.
Check that the page scrolls to that section.
S35.21.where: Report reader > Contents box (above the body)

S35.22.needs: a paid account, a finished report with citations
S35.22.note: The link format was read from the code, not seen on screen; the exact visible look of a citation number was not confirmed.
steps: Open a finished report that has numbered citations in its text.
Click a citation number in the body.
Check that it takes you to or opens its source.
Compare the link with the matching source in the Citations list.
S35.22.where: Report reader > body, numbered citations; Research side panel > Sources tab

S35.23.note: Charts have no control of their own; they appear only when the model writes a chart block, so the tester cannot choose them.
steps: Send a Deep Research question and wait for the Research plan card.
Under Deliverable, open Format and pick Prose with comparison tables.
Start research and open the finished report.
Check that tables render in the body. Charts written as chart blocks render inline in the body.
S35.23.where: Plan card > Deliverable > Format > Prose with comparison tables; then read the report body

S35.25.needs: a paid account, at least one past report (the empty state says No reports yet)
steps: Open the research side panel and click the Library tab.
Read the list of reports, newest first.
Click a report title to reopen it.
Scroll to the end of the list and check for Load older reports.
S35.25.where: Research side panel > Library tab (open from View N sources or the Research sources button)

S35.26.needs: a paid account, a finished report with a question
steps: Open a finished report.
Click Run again in the toolbar.
Look for a new Deep research status card in the chat.
Compare the new run's results with the old report.

S35.28.needs: a paid account, a finished report
steps: Open a finished report.
Click PDF in the toolbar and check that a file downloads.
Repeat with Word and Markdown.
Open each file and compare the title and body with the report.
S35.28.where: Report reader toolbar > Markdown, PDF or Word

S35.31.needs: a paid account, a finished report
S35.31.note: Whether the artifact becomes an interactive page depends on the model; the toolbar button only creates the artifact.
steps: Open a finished report.
Click Artifact in the toolbar.
Look for a new artifact opened from the report.
Check that it can be shown as an interactive web page.

labels.text: Get a notification when this research finishes

S35.33.needs: a paid account, a browser that allows notifications, a run that stays active
S35.33.note: The footer only shows while the run is active and browser permission is still default; push notifications were not checked.
steps: Start a Deep Research run in the browser while the card shows Searching the web.
Click Enable in the footer and allow notifications in the browser prompt.
Wait for the run to finish or fail.
Look for the browser notification and the completed status in the chat.
S35.33.where: Deep research status card > Get a notification when this research finishes > Enable

S35.34.needs: a Free account or a paid account with managed credits; the research plan must be waiting for approval
S35.34.note: The Expected line says runs or credits; the screen shows only a credit amount ("You have X available right now."), with no run count, and the line is hidden when usage data is missing. The item's "Where to find it: not written yet" is outdated because the code exists at apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchCostEstimate.tsx and is used by ResearchActivity.tsx:805. The exact plus-button label was not found in the files read, so the menu opener is described by position only.
steps: Sign in with an account that has managed usage (a paid or Free plan with credits).
In the message box, open the plus (attachment) menu and choose "Research" so it is checked.
Type a research question and send it.
Wait until the "Research plan" card appears and asks you to approve the plan (it is not running yet).
Look under the plan steps for "Estimated cost: up to about ..." and the line "You have ... available right now." Compare the credit amount with the remaining credits you expect.
S35.34.where: Composer plus button > Research (turn on), send a research question, then wait for the "Research plan" card to show its "Start research" button. The line "You have ... available right now." sits above "Start research".
